name: Pectoralis Major Tendon Rupture
definition: Partial or complete rupture of the pectoralis major tendon, usually during forceful eccentric loading such as bench press.

investigations.principle: MRI of the chest/shoulder region defines tear location and retraction; ultrasound may assist.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Complete tendon avulsion in active patients is commonly treated surgically for best strength recovery.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Urah/Amsa-Snayu rupture phenotype may be documented only after modern tendon diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Partial or complete rupture of the pectoralis major tendon, usually during forceful eccentric loading such as bench press.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
